title: Dispatch completed Hostinger build-log evidence through a governed single-use bridge

phases.objective: Rotate the existing single-use GitHub metadata bridge so it dispatches the merged trusted-main completed-build log workflow for the exact Hostinger build UUID, while requiring an explicit current-main SHA and preserving GET-only provider boundaries.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: An explicit repository-owner workflow dispatch or exact governed Issue #4953 comment supplies the current trusted main SHA.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Before the first metadata write, the bridge validates the explicit main SHA, authorization comment, target workflow blob, protected Production SHA, completed build UUID, issue state, and one-time marker absence; it then dispatches the unchanged GET-only completed-build log workflow and records the target run ID.
steps: Resolve the exact expected main SHA from the required workflow_dispatch input or governed issue-comment token.
Validate operator identity, control issue, exact trigger format, and canonical 40-character main SHA.
Validate authorization comment 5162389651 and the immutable target workflow path, blob, account, domain, completed build UUID, Production SHA, and safety boundaries.
Reject execution if current main, Production, target workflow blob, workflow state, issue state, or one-time marker state diverges.
Record one R3B claim comment after all immutable checks pass.
Dispatch the unchanged trusted-main completed-build log workflow with account username, exact build UUID, and expected Production SHA.
Resolve the new workflow_dispatch run for the exact main SHA and record its run ID.
assertions: Every write-capable path requires an explicit expected main SHA and checks it against current main before the first metadata write.
The issue-comment path is exact-token, exact-operator, exact-issue bounded; workflow_dispatch is repository-owner bounded.
The bridge never receives or references secrets.HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN.
Only the target workflow reads the Hostinger token from the configured GitHub secret on trusted main.
The target workflow blob is exactly 94321b273e70f96180c0f058adbb291b035fd237.
The selected build UUID is exactly 019fc51c-3947-7255-aa4d-f55cb8df7658 and the expected Production SHA is exactly f5c1ae8840b4d4452f2908bb0f23051880bb6896.
The bridge writes only claim and dispatch metadata and invokes only the target GitHub Actions workflow.

No Hostinger build creation, deployment, release activation, restart, provider mutation, repository contents mutation, protected-ref update, force push, SQL, migration Apply, database mutation, or external send occurs.
The authorization binding cannot be reused after a claim or dispatch marker exists.

phases.objective: Observe the one-time completed-build log evidence artifact and record its bounded source-provenance classification in Incident #4953.
Confirm the bridge fails closed when the explicit head input, authorization, target workflow blob, current main, Production, build UUID, issue state, or one-time markers diverge.
This bridge performs no Hostinger canary or provider mutation.
This bridge does not deploy, activate, restart, or mutate Production.
